# Input Area

```tsx
import { InputArea } from "@s0l/design-system"
```

A multi-line text field. Mirrors the Figma Input Area component: State (Default / Hover / Active / Disabled / Read Only) × Filled × Error, plus Resizable. Hover, Active and Filled follow the browser; Disabled, Read Only and Error come from props.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<InputArea {...args} icon={getLeadingIcon({ showIcon, icon })} />
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Input Area component: State (Default / Hover / Active / Disabled / Read Only) × Filled × Error, plus Resizable. It shares the label, field, Focus ring and messages with Input Text.
The <textarea> fills the whole field so the browser's resize grip sits in the field corner. Its padding reserves room for the icon, Button Clear and the Resize Area, minus the 1px border Figma draws inside the frame. The native grip is hidden in WebKit/Blink and the Figma Resize Handle is drawn on top, tinted with the border token.

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`InputAreaProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon?` | `IconSvgElement` | Leading 20px icon. |
| `resizable?` | `boolean` | Lets the user resize the field vertically and shows the Resize Handle. |

## Rules

- Import `InputArea` from `@s0l/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
